async def act(page):
    """Navigate directly to the CMS page edit screen for the Home Page and update its Page Title.

    Strategy:
    - Use a relative goto to land on the CMS page edit URL for the Home Page (commonly page_id=1).
    - Use accessibility-oriented selectors (get_by_label / get_by_role) exclusively (no CSS selectors).
    - Fill the Page Title field with the requested string.
    - Click a Save button (make this the final action because it will navigate away).
    """
    # Navigate to the CMS edit page for the Home Page using a relative URL
    await page.goto("/index.php/admin/cms_page/edit/page_id/1/")
    # Wait until network is mostly idle so form elements are available
    await page.wait_for_load_state("networkidle")

    new_title = "This is the home page!! Leave here!!"

    # Try accessibility-first locators for the page title input
    title_locators = [
        page.get_by_label("Page Title"),
        page.get_by_role("textbox", name="Page Title"),
        page.get_by_role("textbox", name="Title"),
        page.get_by_label("Title"),
    ]

    filled = False
    for locator in title_locators:
        try:
            if await locator.count() > 0:
                # Use the first match if multiple
                await locator.nth(0).fill(new_title)
                filled = True
                break
        except Exception:
            # If any locator fails unexpectedly, continue to the next
            continue

    if not filled:
        raise RuntimeError("Unable to locate the CMS page title input using accessibility selectors.")

    # Determine a sensible parent for Save buttons (prefer the form if present)
    parent = page
    form_locator = page.get_by_role("form")
    if await form_locator.count() > 0:
        parent = form_locator.nth(0)

    # Try likely save button names; clicking a save will navigate away so it must be the final action
    save_names = ["Save Page", "Save and Continue Edit", "Save"]
    for name in save_names:
        btn = parent.get_by_role("button", name=name)
        if await btn.count() > 0:
            await btn.nth(0).click()
            return

    # As a last resort try top-level buttons by name (no parent)
    for name in save_names:
        btn = page.get_by_role("button", name=name)
        if await btn.count() > 0:
            await btn.nth(0).click()
            return

    raise RuntimeError("Could not find a Save button on the CMS page edit screen.")

- The previous error was caused by using CSS locators. To fix that, I will only use accessibility selectors: page.get_by_label and page.get_by_role.
- For the Page Title field, get_by_label("Page Title") is the primary choice. I add fallbacks such as get_by_role("textbox", name="Page Title") and variants in case label or role differs slightly.

Step 4: Filling the title.
- After navigating and waiting for networkidle, try the series of accessibility locators and fill the first matching locator with the new title.

Step 5: Saving.
- Clicking a Save control will likely navigate away from the page, so this must be the final action. To reduce ambiguity and follow guidance about nested buttons, I prefer to look for a containing form (page.get_by_role("form")). If found, search inside that form for buttons named "Save Page", "Save and Continue Edit", or "Save" (in that order). If no form is available, try the same button names at the page level.

Step 6: Error handling.
- If the Page Title input cannot be found via accessibility selectors, raise an error explaining that.
- If no Save button is found, raise a descriptive error.
